c5640.summary: Dikshitar's prayer to Krishna as the child Gopala, recounting his form and his deeds.
m: O child Gopala, protect me quickly, loving to devotees, ocean of compassion, Hari,
dark as a rain cloud, steadfast, lotus-handed, giver of matchless bliss, who in play took the guise of a cowherd, bearer of the flute, of Lakshmi, noble Damodara;
expert in slaying the wrestler Chanura, who killed Shakatasura with his foot, slayer of Mura, wearing a ruby crown, necklaces and bracelets,
skilled in splitting the brow of the rutting elephant, worshipped by Brahma, clad in yellow silk, wearing the Vaijayanti forest garland,
whose mind triumphs over the impurities beginning with ego, who destroyed Kamsa, (protector of) Brahmins who bow, destroyer of Drona, Karna, Duryodhana and others, (protector of) Draupadi's
honour, praised by Guruguha, the veena player and singer, worshipped by Shiva, delight of the gopis' hearts.

c5627.summary: A hymn to Shiva as Akshayalinga of Tirukkannapuram/Kizhvelur, lord of countless universes.
m: O Akshayalinga, all-pervading, self-born, lord of countless universes — protect me, Shambhu.

Of imperishable form, of boundless valour, rider of the bull, enchanter of the world, chastiser of Daksha, most skilled, bearing divine marks, unlike all creation, the goal and its definition, deeply wise, who drank the poison, whose glance is the guru's grace;
with the goddess of the Badari forest, lord of Bhadrakali, worshipped by devotees, revered by Vishnu and the gods,
free of the workings of maya, compassionate father of Guruguha, beyond the gunas, surrounded by the good, Shankara, with a heart soft as butter,
radiant, (delighting in) Tumburu's music, born of the syllable Hrim, lord of the golden mountain, wish-tree to those who seek refuge,
whose lotus feet (are worshipped) by Brahma, celebrated in the Chaitra festival with chariots, elephants, horses and foot soldiers, Sadashiva, of the nature of existence, consciousness and bliss.

c5970.summary: Salutations to Subrahmanya, slayer of Taraka and Shurapadma, teacher of the truth, giver of enjoyment and liberation.
m: Salutations, salutations to Sri Subrahmanya, lovely as countless Manmathas, refuge of the humble,

whose lotus feet are worshipped by Brahmins and all people, who took the form of serpents like Vasuki and Takshaka, revered by Indra and all gods, most excellent, foremost among granters of devotees' wishes;
to the destroyer of Taraka, Simhamukha, Shurapadma and other demons, skilled in removing the three afflictions, the teacher of the Truth;
to Guruguha, praised by heroes, a sun to the darkness of ignorance, husband of Valli, bearer of the Shakti spear;
to the steadfast one to whom Brahma bowed, son-in-law of Indra, enjoyer of the worlds beginning with Bhu, giver of enjoyment and liberation.

c1420.summary: Dikshitar takes refuge in Nataraja of Chidambaram, radiant in the dance of bliss.
m: I take refuge in the lord of the Chit Sabha, radiant in the dance of bliss, Lord of Shivakamavalli,
radiant as countless suns, the space in the heart that grants enjoyment and liberation, skilled in protecting the humble, whose raised lotus foot was revealed to Patanjali and Vyaghrapada,
bearer of the moon and the Ganga, blue-throated, support of the holy places beginning with Kedara,
lord of all beings, clad in tiger skin, (dweller in) Chidambaram, lord of the three thousand Brahmin sages,
lord of the universe, with a heart soft as butter, compassionate, father of Guruguha, known through the Vedas, free of attachment,
immeasurable, expounded as non-dual, whose many kinds of tandava born of the joy of music and instruments are a wonder.

c5667.summary: O mind, worship the child Krishna, whose lotus feet grant every wish.
m: O mind, worship Sri Balakrishna, Mukunda, whose lotus feet grant whatever one wishes,

with a body like a fresh rain cloud, young son of Nanda, in yellow robes, with a conch-like neck, who held up the mountain, slayer of Putana and others, incarnation of the Supreme Person, who roams in calm hearts, husband of Sri Rukmini;
whose mouth bears the scent of butter, of gentle speech, with lotus-petal eyes, who lies on a banyan leaf,
with a nose like a fresh champaka bud, shining like the atasi flower, protector of Indra and the guardians who bow to him, with a musk tilaka,
wearing a garland of fresh tulasi, (surrounded by) Narada and hosts of sages, protector of the earth, Gopala praised by Guruguha.

c1286.summary: On the yogic splendour of Tyagaraja (Shiva) of Tiruvarur. The pallavi drops a syllable at each step (gopuchha yati); the madhyamakala builds back up (srotovaha yati).
m: The yogic splendour of Tyagaraja (Shiva of Tiruvarur) — Sadashiva!
The yogic splendour of Tyagaraja — in him I always take refuge.
The yogic splendour of Tyagaraja —
the splendour of the yoga of the king of mountains,
the splendour of royal yoga,
the splendour of yoga,
splendour,
being,
'vam' (the seed syllable).
Whose feet are praised by the king of serpents (Patanjali), abode of nada, bindu and kala,
whose feet are known to the kings of yogis, who grants enjoyment and liberation together,
established in yoga, cause of the creation of the universe of names and forms,
veiled by the cycles of yugas, years, months, days and hours.
Lord of Anandabhairavi, guru of Sri Guruguha, existence-consciousness-bliss,
Shiva, Shakti and all the principles —
the radiance of their very form,
self-radiant,
the radiance of their very form,
the radiance of the form of the principles,
the radiance of the form of all the principles,
the radiance of the form of all the principles beginning with Shiva and Shakti.

c5800.summary: Dikshitar asks Minakshi of Madurai, daughter of the Pandya king and beloved of Sundareshvara, to grant him joy.
m: Minakshi, grant me joy, dark-limbed one, Rajamatangi,
Mother who is the measure of all, Maya, of emerald hue, Shiva's consort, fish-eyed one, releaser from bonds, noble one, dweller in the Kadamba forest,
dwelling in Madurai, wearing jewelled bangles, daughter of the Pandya king Malayadhvaja,
whose face mocks the moon, victorious one, delighting in veena music with its ten gamakas,
whose heart is joyful in the intoxication of spring, compassionate, beloved of Mahadeva Sundareshvara,
sister of Vishnu, slender-waisted, who captivates Brahma and Guruguha, Shankari.

c1057.summary: A hymn to Kamakshi of Kanchipuram as Tripurasundari.
m: Lotus-petal-eyed Kamakshi, Kamalamanohari, Tripurasundari,
of elephant-like gait, with lovely feet adorned with gems, protect me, parrot in Shiva's cage, lotus-faced, delight of Guruguha, destroyer of sins, untainted one,
with a face like the full moon, lovely teeth, protector of Manmatha, dwelling in a jewelled house, clad in gold, gracious one,

whose gentle smile is the home of love, Bhuvaneshvari of the one and many syllables, bringer of the nectar of bliss, radiant, who makes the mind one-pointed and absorbed, giver of good, queen of Ekamresha's house, Shankari.

c5829.summary: A prayer to lotus-eyed Kamakshi, the goddess of the nine enclosures of the Sri Chakra.
m: Lotus-eyed Kamakshi, with hair dark as rain clouds, Tripura,
worshipped by Sharada and Lakshmi, with a face like the lotus and moon, lotus-footed, giver of boons — save me, O abode of truth,
Gauri, radiant in Hindola, with ornaments of diamonds and gems, praised by Vishnu and Brahma, (dwelling in) the nine enclosures made of Shiva and Shakti,
worshipped by the jewels among women and others, whose inner being lies beyond nada, served by the wise, cause of beautiful Guruguha.

c1008.summary: A hymn to Ranganatha of Srirangam as Kodanda Rama, with the raga name woven in.
m: O dweller in Srirangam, victory to you, incarnation as Kodanda Rama, hero of the Raghus,
father of Manmatha, God, giver of boons to the elephant king, dwelling in Lakshmi's heart, dark one,
whose steed is the bird Garuda, of compassionate glance, lover of good company,
moon to the ocean of the Solar race, lotus-faced, Pattabhirama,
whose lotus feet conquered Kama, Raghurama, Lord of Sita who sits at your left side,
reclining on Shesha, delight of devotees, with eyes of moon and sun, of gentle speech,
with spotless mirror-like cheeks, remover of the sages' sorrows,
Govinda, Venkataramana, Mukunda, Sankarshana, root cause, Shankara,
bliss of Guruguha.

c5938.summary: O mind, always worship Krishna — the child Gopala, lord of Guruvayur.
m: O mind, always worship Sri Krishna, protector of those who seek refuge, the child Gopala,
whose feet are praised by Indra and others, remover of sorrow, delusion and fear, the crossing of worldly life,
with conch, discus, mace, lotus and forest garland, delighting in the flute, abode of compassion,
adorned with bracelets, armlets and crown, in lovely golden robes,
revered by Brahma and the gods, worshipped by Sri Guruguha, with Lakshmi,
lotus-petal-eyed, lying on the banyan leaf, lord of Guruvayur, lord of the worlds.

c1123.summary: Worship Balambika of Vaitheeswarankoil, mother of Muttukumara, whose form is the sacred syllables of the Panchadashi mantra.
m: Worship, O mind, Balambika, the wish-fulfilling creeper of devotees,
whose feet readily grant one's true form, the rosy one, eternally auspicious, Sharvani,
born of the Vagbhava kuta, whose form is the four Vedas,
born of the Kamaraja kuta of love, pervading the whole universe,
the Goddess born of the Shakti seed, whose body is the letters of the alphabet,
praised by the gods, dwelling in the heart of Vaidyanatha, lord of physicians, healer of the disease of worldly life,
delighting in bhava, raga and tala, granter of devotees' desires,
protector of those who serve her, mother of Muttukumara, who is Guruguha.

c5954.summary: Victory to Guruguha, first of the gurus; meditate always in the heart, 'I am Chidanandanatha'.
m: Victory, victory to Guruguha, (first among) the gurus beginning with Sri Natha; worship always in your heart, thinking 'I am Chidanandanatha'.

Creator of the diverse universe of name, form and the five elements, a blazing sun to the darkness of ignorance, giver of knowledge, the great lord, most divine, eager to save the humble, who bears all bodies beginning with the divine lineage, delighting the mind, most skilled — may my noble guru grant auspiciousness.
The basis of the universe made of maya, practiser of the 'kadi' tradition, (worshipped) within the Malini mandala
by rite, meditating on the Hamsa japa that begins the mantras, free of the workings of maya, seated on my thousand-petalled
lotus, who drinks the nectar of sweet music, granter of fearlessness and boons to Vishnu and others, of the form of Brahman
variegated by maya, beautiful as countless Manmathas, a lamp in the tower of the hearts of the wise,
whose valour conquered the proud Shura and others, whose feet are worshipped by kings of lands such as Mayamalavagaula,
who illumines Vishnu and the hosts of gods, who taught Shiva the great meaning (of Om).

c1240.summary: Salutations to Kantimati of Tirunelveli, Shankara's young consort and mother of Guruguha.
m: I salute Sri Kantimati, Shankara's young consort, mother of Sri Guruguha,
whose face has the form of the seed syllable Hrim,
whose splendid home is of gold and gems,
praised by Indra and the gods,
daughter of the snow mountain, to whom Parashurama bowed,
always worshipped by Shuka, Shaunaka and others, pure,
dwelling on the banks of the Tamraparni, delighting in the conch and a thousand and eight
pots of sacred ablution, beneficent to the gods.

c1827.summary: A hymn to Varalakshmi, sung for the Varalakshmi vrata on the Friday before the full moon of Shravana.
m: Salutations to Sri Varalakshmi —
to you, giver of wealth,
lotus-footed one, abode of delight,
at once, at every step.
Beloved of Vishnu, father of Manmatha,
of golden radiance,
radiant as ten million suns,
easily reached by devotees,
protector of those who serve you,
wearing a lotus garland,
endowed with pure virtues,
who plays in Keshava's heart.
On the Friday before the full moon of Shravana,
whose form is worshipped by Charumati and others,
wearing a jewelled necklace offered by the gods and Guruguha,
showering gold, skilled in protecting the humble,
skilled in dispelling differences in contemplation, the best, praised by Sarasvati,
intent on granting liberation, whose hands grant the fruits one desires.

c5968.summary: We always worship Satyanarayana, made of truth, knowledge and bliss.
m: We always worship Sri Satyanarayana, made of truth, knowledge and bliss — all is Vishnu,
worshipped by Indra and others, contemplated by hosts of great sages, protector of devotees, dwelling radiant in Badari,
the cause of the merchant's (story), who took the form of a Brahmin boy, gracious in the Kali age, skilled in granting wealth,
glorious in the ten incarnations beginning with the fish, tortoise and boar, holding conch, discus and lotus, renowned, praised by Guruguha.

c5722.summary: Dikshitar worships golden Lakshmi alone and renounces seeking help from lowly men.
m: I always worship golden Lakshmi; I give up seeking refuge in lowly men.
Giver of lasting wealth, daughter of the milk ocean, dwelling on Hari's chest, doe-like, with tender leaf-like feet, holding a lily in her lotus hand, with emerald bangles,
dwelling in Shvetadvipa, Sri Kamalambika, the supreme, delighting in all that was and will be, worshipped by Brahmins, the best,
the Mother wearing a lotus garland and ruby ornaments, delighting in song and instruments, (one with) Girija — that Indira,
whose face is like the cool-rayed moon, dwelling in the wish-jewel house of those who seek refuge, clad in yellow, beloved of Guruguha's uncle (Vishnu), Lalita.

c1191.summary: The first of Dikshitar's Navagraha kritis, addressed to Surya, the Sun.
m: Salutations to you, O form of the Sun, lord of beautiful Chaya,
light of the world of cause and effect, lord of the sign of Leo,
radiance praised by the noble, whose glory grants health and other blessings,
friend of the lotus, Mitra, Bhanu, thousand-rayed, father of Karna,
fire that destroys cruel sins, delighting Guruguha, self-radiant,
praised by the wise, jewel of the day, crest-jewel of the planets beginning with the Moon,
witness of actions, worshipped by the steadfast, rider of the divine seven-horsed chariot,
whose essence is the Saurashtra (seed) mantra, of golden form,
the self of Brahma, Hari and Hara, granter of enjoyment and liberation.

c1188.summary: A prayer to Rama at his coronation (Pattabhirama), seated with Sita in the jewelled pavilion, served by his brothers and allies.
m: Protect me, Pattabhirama — victory! — whose name Hanuman praises,
with tender leaf-like feet, Kodanda Rama, rain-cloud
dark in form, lotus-eyed, all-fulfilled,
beloved Raghurama, Kalyanarama, Rama.
As Bharata holds the umbrella and chamara, as Lakshmana,
Shatrughna, Vibhishana, Sugriva and the chief ones serve you,
worthy of the grace of Atri, Vasishtha and others, son
of Dasharatha, in the hall adorned with Maniranga creepers, the nine-
gem pavilion, on the wondrous jewelled throne,
seated with Sita, of noble deeds, most
holy, friend of Guruguha, moon to the nectar ocean of the Solar race,
ruler of the earth, Ramachandra.

c3575.summary: Dikshitar meditates on Ramachandra, jewel of the Raghu race, lord of Sita.
m: I meditate on Ramachandra, jewel of the Raghu race, Upendra,
Lord of the Earth's daughter, giver of enjoyment and liberation, whose name and kirtana save, best of men, beyond illusion,
dwelling in the city of Saketa, granter of sovereignty, (served by) Hanuman,
with a face like the full moon, the Lord, endowed with lovely auspicious qualities,
Kakutstha, wise, lotus-eyed, glorious,
endless, praised by Shiva, sporting with Guruguha among men.

c5876.summary: A hymn to Ramanatha of Rameshvaram, the Shiva worshipped by Rama.
m: I worship Ramanatha, worshipped by Ramachandra,
the god who grants desired fruits, whose power equals ten million holy waters, known to Kumara Guruguha, praised by hosts of monkeys and others,
who roams on Gandhamadana hill by the bridge, ever delighting the heart of Parvatavardhini,
as plain as a gooseberry in the hand, the best, wearing golden necklaces, remover of sins like murder, of the form of 'Hamsa — So'ham'.

c5634.summary: A prayer to Annapurna of Kashi, consort of Vishveshvara, who holds a vessel of payasam and a golden ladle.
m: Annapurne, wide-eyed one, witness of all the worlds, protect me with your glance,
who roams on the banks of the deep Ganga, embodiment of Om, remover of sins, queen adorned with serpents, ancient one, radiant consort of Vishveshvara, the supreme Lord,
whose hands hold a ruby vessel filled with payasam and a golden ladle,
most skilled in protecting Manmatha and others, wearing golden ornaments and garments,
the supreme one, served by Brahma and others, praised by Tumburu, Narada and others,
skilled in granting liberation beyond the three gunas, radiant in three words, loving to Guruguha.

c5647.summary: Dikshitar worships the young Subrahmanya, son of Shiva and Parashakti, who rides the peacock.
m: I worship Balasubrahmanya, the wish-fulfilling tree for devotees,
who delights the heart of blue-throated Shiva, eternal, pure, awakened, free, sky-clad,
bearing the spear, beautiful, skilled in teaching the meaning of Vedanta, Guruguha incarnate (son) of the fire-eyed one,
Parashakti's tender son, steadfast, protector of the hosts of gods, (beyond) the illusion of the five elements,
rider of the blue-throated peacock, of beautiful body, a stream of unsurpassed bliss.

c5958.summary: A hymn to Rajagopala of Mannargudi (Dakshina Dvaraka), with Rukmini and Satyabhama at his sides.
m: Sri Rajagopala, child sporting in love, protector of those who seek refuge,
foremost of the steadfast, refuge of the humble, dwelling in lovely Champakaranya, Dakshina Dvaraka, abode of Vishishtadvaita and Advaita — protect me.
Smiling-faced, whom four-faced Brahma serves, whose divine saving name Narayana is recited by
Narada and others, lotus-footed, ever joyful, who took a woman's form, Murari, Hari, king of Sri Vidya,
with Rukmini and Satyabhama at either side, whose neck surpasses the conch, on the banks of the brimming Haridra river,
Madhava of the great festival, father of Manmatha, bowed to by Shuka, Sanaka and Janaka, valiant, honoured by Guruguha, with Lakshmi.

c5782.summary: Protect me, Minakshi, who holds a ruby veena and whose braid is dark as a swarm of bees.
m: Protect me, Minakshi, Rajamatangi, holding a ruby veena, of sweet speech, whose braid is like a swarm of bees,
embodiment of the joyous spirit of Somasundareshvara, dark one, Shankari, glorious conqueror of the directions,
adorned with gold and gem ornaments, dwelling in the heart of Isha and Guruguha, a stream that grants desired things,
full of the nectar of compassion, remover of desire, anger and the rest, roaming in the Kadamba forest.

c5929.summary: Dikshitar's first kriti, composed at Tiruttani: 'I am the servant of Guruguha — or else, I am Guruguha himself.'
m: I am the servant of Sri Guruguha — if not, I am Guruguha, pure consciousness, myself;
(servant) of him whose feet are enjoyment and liberation, of the nine enclosures beginning with the earth-square, of the inner minds of hosts of yogis, cause of the yoga seat and all else;
whose blissful form is praised by Sanaka and the ancient sages, who grants Brahma and all the gods
their desires, who destroys the works of ignorance — the world of birth and death —
whose home is the hearts of great souls steadfast in reflection, meditation and samadhi, radiant as ten million suns,
the luminous lord of the world, who delights people, the best, higher than all, Hara.
